text:
Sam: FYI converted 'eleuther/psi-7b' -> redwood model and saw repeated fallback to slow tokenizer during evaluation. fast tokenizer files present in HF repo but loader picks the slow path.
Morgan: Can you paste the loader log?
Sam: paste logs below
DevBot: ERROR: tokenizer loader: no 'tokenizer.json' found in /models/psi-7b/fast_tokenizer -> falling back to slow tokenizer
Sam: but there is a tokenizer.json in the HF release tarball: `tokenizer.json` + `tokenizer_config.json` are both in the archive.
Carla: Hmm. We recently changed priority to prefer `tokenizer_config.json` when present (PR #4129) because some HF models ship only `tokenizer_config.json` with slow-tokenizer metadata. That might have regressed for mixed packages.
Alice: This surfaced in quantization runs too. When we ran INT4 experiments the fast-tokenizer route was missing specials and eval BLEU/ROUGE dropped ~2-3 pts. Looks like the fast loader didn't pick up `special_tokens_map` from tokenizer.json because it read tokenizer_config first and assumed slow-tokenizer semantics.
Ben: I think two separate issues: (1) loader priority logic (tokenizer.json vs tokenizer_config.json) and (2) a missing mapping step for fast->slow special tokens when only partial metadata present.
Rachel: Can someone share a minimal repro? I can add a guard in CI after that.
Sam: repro steps:
```
# simplified
mkdir /tmp/psi
tar -xvf psi-7b.tar -C /tmp/psi
# files present:
# tokenizer.json
# tokenizer_config.json
# special_tokens_map.json
python convert_to_redwood.py /tmp/psi --out /models/psi-7b
# then run small eval harness
python eval_promptset.py --model /models/psi-7b --prompts smoke.json
```
Sam: Observed loader log shows it reads tokenizer_config.json first, sets `is_fast=false`, then never attempts to load tokenizer.json.
Morgan: Ok that matches my hunch. The loader uses a triage: if tokenizer_config has `tokenizer_class: <SomeSlowClass>` we short-circuit. We should change to: if tokenizer.json exists, prefer fast tokenizer; else consult tokenizer_config.json.
Carla: Agree. Also preserve backwards compat: if tokenizer.json absent but tokenizer_config explicitly lists a fast class, we should try to construct a fast tokenizer from the config.
Ben: Quick patch idea: reorder checks, then validate that required fields (e.g., `special_tokens_map`, `added_tokens`) are consistent across files. If inconsistent, emit a loader warning and prefer tokenizer.json for runtime.
Alice: For the quant experiments we need a test: run conversion + evaluation for a small promptset and assert no drop > 1% when switching quantized backends. I'll add a smoke eval step to the quant pipeline.
Rachel: I'll add CI job: `hf-token-compat-smoke` that runs on new model imports. Failing job blocks merges to `eng-ml` for loader changes.
DevBot: Deploy checklist created: issue #5582, assigned to @Carla.
Carla: I'll open PR to change loader order + add warning + unit tests. Plan: patch, small canary roll to staging, run internal evals (n=2k prompts) and then promote. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Sam: Thanks. Priorities: (1) fix loader order, (2) add parity check for special tokens, (3) CI smoke for model imports.
Ben: Also add a telemetry metric when loader falls back to slow: `tokenizer.load.fallback_slow` with model name + reason. Helps catch future regressions.
Sam: Sounds good. @Rachel can you own the CI job?
Rachel: Yep, I'll create the job and add to the PR checklist.
Sam: Great. Closing loop here — please post PR link when ready and tag this thread. :thumbsup:
